text:
kai: Heads up — seeing nondeterministic eval results on the quantized-m2 bringup in CI. Same seed/config but scores jitter across runs. anyone else hit this?

maria: yup noticed it on the nightly: 3 runs w/ identical prompts, Rouge-L 0.82 / 0.79 / 0.83. sometimes metric becomes NaN for one shard.

anita: could be sampling params not being enforced by the harness, or RNGs not fully seeded (numpy/py random/torch). also quant kernels can be nondet on GPU.

sam: do we have the exact generation config getting logged? iirc eval-runner prints a partial config but not top_k/top_p/temperature explicitly for each example.

kai: current harness block in repo: ```generation_config = {"temperature": 0.7, "top_p": 0.9, "seed": 42}``` but actual sampling call uses model.sample(..., sampler=Sampler()) where Sampler uses np.random if torch tensor path not taken.

maria: aha. sampler code: ```if isinstance(input, np.ndarray): np.random.choice(...)
else: torch.multinomial(...)``` so seed propagation mismatch possible.

anita: checklist we should run through:
- ensure we call random.seed(seed), np.random.seed(seed), torch.manual_seed(seed)
- set torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) or torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True (aware this may hurt perf)
- disable dropout and any stochastic augmentations in eval path
- log full generation_config and backend/quantization metadata per run

ci-bot: CI pipeline 8452: flaky-tests marker added to job "eval/quantized-m2-nightly" (see: <https://ci.redwood.example/8452>)

eval-runner: quick log dump from run 8452: ```seed=42, temp=0.7, top_p=0.9, sampler=autoreg, backend=awq-int8, device=gpu:0
example_id=abcd1234 output_hash=0x7f3a2c metric=0.79
example_id=abcd1234 output_hash=0x7f4b91d metric=0.83``` suggests small binary differences in output leading to metric diff.

sam: could be float rounding/quant noise flipping token probabilities early in sequence, causing drift. even a tiny change can cascade.

kai: agreed. Also noticed different CUDA/cuDNN versions in self-hosted runners vs prod GPU hosts. cudnn nondet ops documented.

maria: pragmatic plan:
1) add strict-deterministic mode behind env var EVAL_DETERMINISTIC=1 that enforces global seeding and deterministic algos (to validate whether nondet comes from RNG vs other sources)
2) expand logging: per-run model_version, quant_backend, CUDA/cuDNN version, generation_config (explicitly top_k/top_p/temperature/seed), and a short output hash
3) create small repro that runs the same prompt N times on same hardware and compares hashes
4) add CI matrix job that toggles quant backends (fp16, int8-awq, nf4) and deterministic mode to isolate failures

anita: i'll open a PR to add the env var + seed propagation hooks into eval-runner. will also add a CLI flag --deterministic.

sam: i'll spin up the repro script and test locally on my workstation (gpu: p4) and on the staging host. aiming to reproduce the drift.

kai: i'll add the extra logging to the runner and ensure generation_config is dumped per-eval. also will include hash(modeled_output) and raw first-8-tokens to help diff.

maria: once we have deterministic vs non-deterministic runs, we can decide whether CI should enforce deterministic for evals (safer but may hide perf regressions tied to nondet kernels).

eval-runner: note: quantized kernels (AWQ/QLoRA int8) may reorder computation for perf -> nondet. we should attach quantization metadata (bit-width, block-size) to logs.

ci-bot: action items created: ISSUE-1214 (add deterministic mode), TASK-2042 (CI matrix for quant backends), TASK-2043 (repro script)

maria: ETA for PRs?

anita: PR for seed propagation + --deterministic in draft today, ready for review tomorrow.

sam: repro script by EOD tomorrow, will post results in this thread.

kai: logging PR up later today. i'll also run the nightly with EVAL_DETERMINISTIC=1 to see if scores stabilize.

maria: perfect — assign owners to the CI tasks once PRs land. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sam: quick note: if deterministic mode fixes flakiness, we still need to understand production behaviour (we can't force deterministic kernels in prod). goal is to identify whether tiny numeric diff source is quantization or RNG.

kai: exactly. deterministic mode is for triage not necessarily for permanent enforcement.

maria: ack. filing a tiny eval test that asserts identical outputs under deterministic mode and fails the job so we don't regress on that.

anita: added that assertion to PR draft; it will only run when EVAL_DETERMINISTIC=1.

kai: awesome. we'll reconvene after the CI matrix completes.

maria: thanks — keeping this thread pinned for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
